description: Can PatchAhead read a release note correctly? Each case is a realistic snippet plus the kind and symbols a correct reading yields. Cases that PatchAhead should refuse are included on purpose: a classifier scored only on what it can do is not a classifier.

cases.text:
### Pagination is now cursor-based

- **Before (v1):** `GET /orders?page=1` returned `page` and `total_pages`.
- **After (v2):** `GET /orders?cursor=<cursor>` returns `next_cursor` and `has_more`.
- The `page` and `total_pages` response fields have been **removed**.

### Cursor pagination

We have moved to cursor-based pagination. Pass `cursor` and read `next_cursor`; keep going while `has_more` is true.

### Order field renamed: `total` -> `amount`

The monetary field on each `order` object was renamed.

### Customer schema

The field renamed `name` to `full_name` on the `customer` object. Update any code reading `customer.name`.

### Client method renamed

The method renamed `fetch_orders` -> `list_orders`. The deprecated `client.fetch_orders()` was removed in v2.

### Keyword argument renamed: `timeout_seconds` -> `timeout`

The `timeout_seconds` keyword argument on `fetch_orders` was renamed to `timeout`.

### Parameter rename

The `retries` parameter was renamed to `max_retries` on `send`. Calls using `retries=` will raise a TypeError.

### Orders endpoint moved

The endpoint moved from `/orders` to `/v2/orders`. Update your base URL.

### Response shape changed

The response shape changed: orders are now nested under a `data` key instead of at the top level.

### Authentication

Authentication has changed from API keys to OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens.

### Performance improvements

We improved response times by 40% and fixed several typos in the documentation.

### Cleanup

Some things were renamed. See the migration guide on our website for details.
cases.note: A rename with no extractable symbols must not be reported as an actionable rename.
